questions.q: What explains minority rule, according to the summary?
a: The majority is flexible or indifferent about the choice
The minority has much more money to spend
The majority is not allowed to vote
The minority controls most of the media
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a small inflexible group wins when everyone else does not care.

questions.q: Which example does the summary use to show minority rule?
a: Most UK lamb imports are halal though only 4% are Muslim
Most cars sold in the US are electric
Most British tea comes from India
Most fast food is bought by teenagers
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that non-Muslim buyers do not mind halal meat.

questions.q: In which fields does image matter more than proven results?
a: CEOs, politicians and bankers
Surgeons, soldiers and lawyers
Authors, athletes and chefs
Engineers, pilots and farmers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says these roles depend on being perceived as capable.

questions.q: Why can a sloppy-looking lawyer still be trusted?
a: Clients keep hiring her only if she keeps winning
Lawyers are judged on appearance alone
Law firms protect their own employees
Clients rarely check a lawyer's results
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the poorly dressed lawyer as proof that results matter where they can be measured.

questions.q: Why are rich people easier to scam?
a: A small loss matters little, so sellers gain more than buyers
They have less access to useful information
They are less able to compare prices
They are more trusting by nature
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the risk-reward ratio tilts toward the seller as wealth grows.
